scope: Optional journaled frontmatter write-back with source-hash tracking; not full M4 acceptance
checks: Write-back is off by default. Enabling it is an administrator setting with session step-up; only owned Markdown files are eligible.
The sandbox inspects frontmatter. The daemon preserves original UTF-8 bytes outside a strict generated section and validates the complete output again in the sandbox.
Authored fields, tag overrides and body text are retained, including BOM, CRLF, Unicode and empty frontmatter. Authored collisions, unsafe YAML and dishonest replacement ranges are rejected.
Journal preparation revalidates job, source, revision/generation and active write-back policy. One enrichment revision records the effect. Interrupted rename recovery is idempotent.
A concurrent managed-file replacement survives as a conflict. External paths are untouched. A repeat enrichment request does not add a revision or model call.
Existing results can be written under administrator authority without another model call, even after the original capture credential is revoked. Fresh inference retains its read/infer requirements.
Backfills of completed jobs obey queue capacity; admission rejection does not terminate the worker.
Source hashes are independent from managed-file hashes. Import and index source scans keep unchanged enriched copies, import changed source bytes and preserve identity/enrichment through moves.
Version six upgrades require a complete encrypted backup before the source-hash column is added; the portable export column policy was reviewed.
Desktop and phone checks cover opt-in, saved state, repeat requests, downloaded file, reading view and lossless view. Four screenshots were reviewed; no workflow console warnings/errors.
limitations: This checkpoint does not implement native provider batch execution or the remaining provider adapters.
The browser and file scenarios use synthetic content and a controlled model; separate earlier evidence covers the actual local enrichment model.
Full daemon restore under sustained edits, mounted external-root and large-corpus qualification, hardened deployment, release operations and remaining real-export acceptance are still open.
